title: Identification of somatic and psychosocial late and long-term effects and associated risk factors in long-term survivors of acute myeloid leukemia - a foundation for evidence-based follow up care
summary:
The AML CARE study aims to understand and address the long-term health effects and quality of life issues in adults who have survived Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). As more people are being cured of AML, there is a growing need to identify and manage the late effects of the disease and its treatments.
The study will recruit a large group of AML survivors (>5 years past their leukemia diagnosis) from two national patient registries and collect detailed information through questionnaires and data from routine medical exams. This will include assessing physical and mental health, as well as identifying any chronic health problems such as heart issues, diabetes, or secondary cancers.
The researchers will also develop predictive models to identify individuals at high risk for these late effects and create screening tools to help in early detection. This study will include patients who have received newer AML treatments, which were not studied before, to see how these treatments impact long-term health.
The goal is to improve the follow-up care and overall health and quality of life for AML survivors. The study involves several clinical centers in Germany and is part of a larger cooperative research project.

interventions.name:
AML long-term survivor cohort
We will perform a cross-sectional questionnaire-based survey of medical and psycho-social late and long-term effects and collect medical data from recent follow-up visits

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Persons who have been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia.
Survival since the initial diagnosis of leukemia ≥ 5 years
Exclusion criteria:
Current hematological relapse
Lack of capacity to give informed consent
Insufficient German language skills that impair the understanding of the written study materials or prevent independent completion of the questionnaire
